### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.clue

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

Whenever I start to record a macro, `mini.clue` is disabled which is the desired behavior.

However, if I open a new buffer or a new file with the `e` command, basically add a buffer that was not available before starting to record a macro, mini.clue is enabled for the new buffer which messes up my macro.
More specifically, pasting from a register for the second time and onwards pastes twice for some reason when replaying a macro(in recording, it is pasted once).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33c475af-a53d-4997-9ab6-1c8b587492f7

### Expected behavior
`mini.clue` is disabled globally until I finish recording the macro.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
   local miniclue = require('mini.clue')
   miniclue.setup({
   triggers = {
     -- Leader triggers
     { mode = 'n', keys = '<Leader>' },
     { mode = 'x', keys = '<Leader>' },

     -- `[` and `]` keys
     { mode = 'n', keys = '[' },
     { mode = 'n', keys = ']' },

     -- Built-in completion
     { mode = 'i', keys = '<C-x>' },

    -- `g` key
    { mode = 'n', keys = 'g' },
    { mode = 'x', keys = 'g' },

    -- Marks
    { mode = 'n', keys = "'" },
    { mode = 'n', keys = '`' },
    { mode = 'x', keys = "'" },
    { mode = 'x', keys = '`' },

    -- Registers
    { mode = 'n', keys = '"' },
    { mode = 'x', keys = '"' },
    { mode = 'i', keys = '<C-r>' },
    { mode = 'c', keys = '<C-r>' },

    -- Window commands
    { mode = 'n', keys = '<C-w>' },

     -- `z` key
     { mode = 'n', keys = 'z' },
     { mode = 'x', keys = 'z' },
   },

    clues = {
      -- Enhance this by adding descriptions for <Leader> mapping groups
      miniclue.gen_clues.square_brackets(),
      miniclue.gen_clues.builtin_completion(),
      miniclue.gen_clues.g(),
      miniclue.gen_clues.marks(),
      miniclue.gen_clues.registers(),
      miniclue.gen_clues.windows(),
      miniclue.gen_clues.z(),
    },
   })

    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Replace this with description of interactive reproduction steps along with the behavior you observe.
   Feel free to include images/videos/etc, this helps a lot.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

I can reproduce, but I'd appreciate (in the future) a written sequence of steps. Here is how it could have looked:
- Place cursor on any word.
- Press `qq` to start recording macro in register `q`.
- Type `yiw`, `:enew<CR>`, `i`, `<C-r>0`.
- Press `q` to stop recording.
- Press `Q` (or `@q`). It executes the same sequence of steps, but in a new buffer the word is inserted twice.

I'll take a look, but I'd not have hopes up, as this part of 'mini.clue' - Neovim inter-operation is pretty hacky.

This should now be resolved on latest `main`. The issue was that creating and focusing new buffer still auto-created triggers which interfered with macro recording. A more global prevention of trigger creation was needed (so, thankfully, not a huge hack).

title: Mini.clue is triggered when recording a macro after opening a new buffer.
